title: arXiv physics weekly: notable recent papers | 14–20 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from cross-subfield listings, research evidence, and revisions, not readership or downloads. Citation evidence is sparse for such recent work and cannot establish popularity.

sections.title: 4D-TEMPO: Differentiable 4D-STEM ptychography via fast Physics Optimizers
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a differentiable physical renderer that fits atoms, microscope, and detector directly to 4D-STEM counts, returning per-atom Fisher-information uncertainties and improving tested reconstructions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report improved atomic-position errors on simulated WSe₂, better held-out-pattern prediction on experimental WSe₂, and faster benchmark runs, with model-conditional per-atom error bars.
sections.evidence_type: computational; multislice/Poisson-likelihood analysis of simulated WSe₂ and experimental WSe₂ and PrScO₃ 4D-STEM data
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say model error can exceed nominal shot-noise ellipses; on real data, individual atoms within one layer are not resolved in depth, and the error bars are conditional on the physical model.

sections.title: Measurements of inclusive J/ψ production in Au+Au collisions at √sNN = 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV with the STAR experiment
sections.abstract: The STAR Collaboration measures mid-rapidity inclusive J/ψ production at four RHIC collision energies and reports centrality and transverse-momentum trends in the nuclear modification factor.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report RAA near 0.5 in the 0–20% centrality class, a hint of increasing RAA with pT at 14.6–27 GeV, and no significant integrated central-collision energy dependence within uncertainties.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; STAR dielectron-channel analysis of Au+Au collision data collected at RHIC
sections.unique_caveat: Reported per-bin systematic uncertainties span 6.5–20.6%, dominated by tracking efficiency; the comparison uses an interpolated p+p reference, and the low-energy trend is described as a hint.

sections.title: Certified Discovery of Quantum Phase Diagrams
sections.abstract: The authors give quantum and classical algorithms that map phase diagrams of geometrically local Hamiltonian families and provide verifiable certificates for detected transitions, with numerical demonstrations on model systems.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that, under stated assumptions, a frequency-filtered local probe can certify transitions and a quantum algorithm can recover phase structure to prescribed resolution without supplied order parameters or training labels.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical and computational; algorithmic proofs plus numerical experiments on model quantum systems
sections.unique_caveat: The guarantee assumes at least one valid reference-ground-state preparation in each gapped region and finite resolvable gaps; sufficiently small gaps, including some first-order transitions, can evade the detection regime.

sections.title: Compiling Constraints into Neuromorphic Ising Machines
sections.abstract: The authors encode combinatorial constraints as programmable transitions in a neuromorphic Ising machine and report optimization and surface-code-decoding benchmarks, including a real-time FPGA implementation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report fewer iterations than penalty-based machines on third-order graph matching and real-time surface-code decoding on FPGA up to distance 9 under noisy syndrome measurements.
sections.evidence_type: computational; neuromorphic Ising-machine benchmarks and FPGA sampler/decoder implementation
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparisons concern specified optimization and surface-code benchmarks and finite code distances; they do not establish general scaling or broad superiority across problem classes.

sections.title: Characterizing a neutral atom quantum simulator accessible in cloud
sections.abstract: The authors experimentally probe Pasqal’s cloud-accessible Fresnel neutral-atom simulator, identify noise sources, and build an effective noisy-dynamics model that reproduces the tested behavior.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that an effective model with numerically inferred noise strengths reproduces the simulator’s observed dynamics for the tested pulse sequences and settings.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; cloud-accessed Pasqal Fresnel neutral-atom analog quantum simulator, with numerical noise-model fitting
sections.unique_caveat: The fitted noise model is tied to Fresnel and the pulse sequences/settings examined; transfer to other devices or operating regimes is not established by this study.

sections.title: Dark Matter Model Implications of a Candidate Sub-halo Near the Sun, and the Data Needed to Discriminate Among Them
sections.abstract: The authors interpret a candidate local mass concentration in pulsar-timing accelerations across several dark-matter models and identify observations that could distinguish the possibilities.
sections.claimed_result: The authors argue that current accelerations leave the candidate’s internal profile, velocity, and population degenerate, and outline tests using interior accelerations, lensing/accretion, emission morphology, and a comoving stellar population.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; phenomenological analysis of existing pulsar-timing acceleration claims and proposed observational tests
sections.unique_caveat: The paper treats the sub-halo as a candidate, not an established detection; the existing acceleration measurements lie outside the tidal radius and cannot determine the inner mass profile.

sections.title: Orbital differentiation in a rare earth ion near half filling
sections.abstract: Using full-multiplet calculations for SmN, the authors report distinct orbital-stiffness subspaces in the ground-state manifold and compare calculated observables with magnetic-susceptibility, neutron-scattering, and DFT results.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find orbital differentiation within the SmN ground J=5/2 manifold and suggest it may support a proposed unconventional triplet-superconductivity interpretation.
sections.evidence_type: computational; full-multiplet crystal-field calculations with Quanty, compared with susceptibility and inelastic-neutron data and DFT spin-density predictions
sections.unique_caveat: The superconductivity connection is suggestive rather than demonstrated, and the inferred orbital structure depends on the crystal-field model and parameter choices.

sections.title: Run it Back: Autoregression vs. Video Diffusion for Final-Conditioned Weather Trajectories
sections.abstract: The revised paper compares a backward autoregressive climate emulator with video diffusion for final-conditioned trajectories of three extreme-weather cases and reports improved variance and physical consistency alongside rollout instability.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that Rewind-AR better captures leading precursor variability and heatwave intensification than the earlier diffusion approach for the examined cases, without the same near-conditioning geostrophic inconsistency.
sections.evidence_type: computational; Rewind-AR/FourCastNet 3 ensembles evaluated against ERA5 for the 2021 Pacific Northwest heatwave, Hurricane Ian, and Superstorm Sandy
sections.unique_caveat: Up to 22% of generated members become numerically unstable within a 66-hour horizon, and the evaluation is based on three cases rather than a broad extreme-event sample.
